activity.notes: Afonso de Albuquerque became the second governor of Portuguese India in 1509 and remained in office until 1515. During that governorship he established the strategic system centered on Goa, Malacca and Hormuz that made him a foundational figure of Portugal's Indian Ocean empire. ATLAS records his formal governorship rather than a generic Portugal-only activity.

sources.title: Albuquerque, Alfonso de — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Encyclopaedia Iranica identifies Afonso de Albuquerque as the second governor of Portuguese India from 1509 to 1515 and as a principal founder of the Portuguese empire in the East.
